display.purpose: Page titles, greeting headlines, brand name. Geometric confidence with warmth.

body.purpose: All running text, descriptions, paragraph content. Invisible workhorse.

mono.purpose: Section headers (// LABEL), timestamps, badges, countdowns, code-adjacent data. Console signature.

shadows.name: panel-resting
shadows.purpose: Default shadow on all glass panels. Subtle ambient lift.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Amber-tinted glow on hovered cards. Signals interactivity.

shadows.name: modal-overlay
shadows.purpose: Full-screen dark overlay with blur for modals.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (hover, focus, theme toggle).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Used for fade-in entrance animations. Decelerates from off-screen.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover/focus state transitions on buttons, links, interactive elements.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary action button. Amber background, dark text, bold weight.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.4rem; background: var(--primary); color: #1a130d; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.15s ease, opacity 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--primary-hover); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action button. Glass surface background with border.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.4rem; background: var(--surface); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--surface-border); border-radius: 10px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface-hover); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive action button. Translucent rose background with rose text and border.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.4rem; background: rgba(248, 113, 113, 0.12); color: var(--error); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--error) 45%, transparent); border-radius: 10px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: rgba(248, 113, 113, 0.22); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--error); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text input field. Glass surface background, amber focus border.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 0.7rem 0.85rem; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--surface-border); background: var(--surface); color: var(--foreground); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.9rem; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--primary); background: var(--surface-hover); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--foreground-muted); }

components.name: Amber Badge
components.description: Amber-toned status badge. Pill shape, monospace uppercase text.
components.css: .ds-badge-amber { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.3rem; padding: 0.18rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 999px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.66rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--primary); background: var(--primary-glow); }

components.name: Teal Badge
components.description: Teal-toned status badge. Same shape as amber badge with teal colors.
components.css: .ds-badge-teal { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.3rem; padding: 0.18rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 999px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.66rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--secondary); background: var(--secondary-glow); }

components.name: Glass Card
components.description: Standard glassmorphic container. Semi-transparent with backdrop blur and resting shadow.
components.css: .ds-glass-card { background: var(--surface); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px); border: 1px solid var(--surface-border); border-radius: 16px; padding: 1.5rem; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0 2px 4px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); transition: transform 0.18s ease, box-shadow 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease; } .ds-glass-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 10px 28px -10px rgba(242, 166, 59, 0.18); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 45%, transparent); }

components.name: Section Header
components.description: Monospace section header with // prefix in amber. Signature visual element.
components.css: .ds-section-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; margin-top: 2.4rem; margin-bottom: 0.9rem; } .ds-section-header h2 { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--foreground-muted); margin: 0; } .ds-section-header h2 span { color: var(--primary); }

components.name: Progress Bar
components.description: Gradient progress track. Teal-to-amber gradient fills a rounded muted track.
components.css: .ds-progress-track { height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface-hover); overflow: hidden; } .ds-progress-bar { height: 100%; border-radius: 999px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--secondary), var(--primary)); transition: width 0.6s ease; }

narrative.overview:
Coffee & Code is a student console that feels like opening your laptop at a premium indie café: warm amber light filtering through glass, the quiet hum of a terminal in the background, and every surface within arm's reach. The design marries coffee-culture warmth (caramel, espresso, cream) with developer-tool precision (monospace labels, terminal-green accents, a console-like shell). Glassmorphism provides depth through translucent layers that let the ambient background glow through, while subtle shadows ground interactive elements and signal hover states.

The system is deliberately dual-natured: a dark espresso mode that feels like a late-night coding session, and a light cream mode that feels like a sunlit study afternoon. Both share the same amber-teal accent pair and glass material, differing only in their neutral ramp. The console metaphor — status bar, side rail, tab bar, monospace section headers with // prefixes — is not decoration; it is the product's identity.
keyCharacteristics: Coffee-caramel-amber primary with terminal-teal secondary — a warm/cool accent pair that never competes
Glassmorphic surfaces with backdrop-filter blur as the primary depth language, grounded by subtle shadows on interactive elements
Console shell metaphor: status bar, side rail (desktop), tab bar (mobile), monospace // section headers
Tactile, confident interactions — clear hover states, visible focus rings, responsive press feedback
Dual-theme: dark espresso default with light cream fallback, both sharing the same accent vocabulary

rules.name: The Warmth Rule
rules.body: No neutral in the system is achromatic. Backgrounds carry brown, text carries cream, borders carry warm white. Pure black, pure white, and pure gray appear nowhere in the palette.

rules.name: The Two-Accent Ceiling
rules.body: Amber and teal are the only accent hues. Status colors (success, warning, error) are functional, not decorative — they appear only in their semantic context and never as a third accent.

rules.name: The Comment Prefix Rule
rules.body: Every section header uses the // label monospace pattern with // in amber. This is not decoration — it is the visual signature that makes the console feel like a codebase. Never drop the //, never change its color from amber, never use it on non-section-header text.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: All time displays, countdowns, and numeric data use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums via the .mono utility. Numbers in columns must align.

rules.name: The Glass-First Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are glass by default. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, focus) or as the resting panel shadow. Glass is the material; shadow is the signal.

dos: Do use the // comment prefix on every section header — it is the signature visual element.
Do keep the amber-teal accent pair exclusive. Status colors are functional, never decorative.
Do use glassmorphism for surfaces that float over the ambient background gradient.
Do add the resting panel shadow to all glass panels — depth without shadows reads as flat.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on all time and number displays.
Do maintain the warm neutral ramp — no achromatic blacks, whites, or grays.
Do use the 10px radius for interactive elements, 16px for containers, 999px for pills.
donts: Don't use pure black (#000) or pure white (#fff) anywhere — the palette is always warm.
Don't use gray for secondary text — tint it toward the warm neutral (muted tan in dark, muted brown in light).
Don't drop the // prefix from section headers or change its color.
Don't add a third accent color — amber and teal are the complete accent vocabulary.
Don't use glassmorphism as pure decoration on elements that don't float over a background gradient.
Don't use border-left above 1px on cards or list items (the 3px accent border on CurrentClass is a featured-panel exception).
Don't mix font families — Space Grotesk is display-only, Inter is body-only, JetBrains Mono is data/label-only.
Don't use modals for tasks that don't need interruption or protected focus.
